tools.name: register_principal
tools.description: Register a principal or gateway identity in PrincipalRegistry. Pass natural metadata/capabilities; publicKey, peerIdHash, metadataURI, metadataHash, and capabilitiesHash are auto-derived when omitted.

tools.name: update_principal
tools.description: Update an existing principal identity and network metadata. Pass peerId to rotate the network identity atomically; peerIdHash is derived and must equal keccak256(UTF-8 peerId).

tools.name: set_provider_passport
tools.description: Publish or update the on-chain Provider Passport reference used for reputation, trust, and settlement identity. Passport document, roots, URI, and hash are auto-generated/uploaded when omitted.

tools.name: publish_provider_resource
tools.description: One-call provider onboarding and publication. Communication-enabled sensors, streams, robots, and interactive resources verify or repair the signing wallet's Principal peer binding before the Manifest is published. Agent services default to asynchronous Provider Connector delivery, fixed listed pricing, and acceptance_required settlement: delivery does not release payment until explicit requester acceptance or arbitration, with no revision right unless the Provider explicitly offers maxRevisions in the Manifest. A response SLA never auto-pays. API/MCP/database resources keep automatic settlement. Set deterministicOutput=true only for an objectively deterministic asynchronous Agent. The signing wallet's primary principal is reused or created automatically.

tools.name: register_resource_address
tools.description: Free-register a transferable permanent Agent Internet Resource Address and bind it to an active provider principal plus Resource Manifest. Pass manifest as JSON and the SDK will derive a data URI plus canonical manifestHash when no storage provider or manifestURI is configured.

tools.name: update_resource_address
tools.description: Update the manifest/passport binding for a Resource Address you own.

tools.name: transfer_resource_address
tools.description: Transfer a Resource Address to another owner wallet, enabling secondary sales.

tools.name: list_resource_addresses
tools.description: List chain-registered Resource Addresses as agent-readable JSON. Results include name, summary, capability, pricing, request/delivery flow, provider, trust, howToUse, and verification anchors; hashes live under verification instead of being the main interface.

tools.name: search_resources
tools.description: Search the complete relevant Resource Address catalog without creating a quote, Intent, escrow, Session, or invocation. Returns a paginated resources set, total match count, facets, nextOffset, and a separate top-five comparison. Use limit/offset to read every matching resource; ranking is not purchase authorization.

tools.name: search_resource_catalog
tools.description: Exhaustive read-only catalog search for questions such as 'which tactile-sensor research Agents exist?' or 'list all Singapore logistics resources'. Returns every relevant match through explicit limit/offset pagination, structured region/type/tag filters, total/count/hasMore/nextOffset, facets, and top-five recommendations. Continue with nextOffset until hasMore=false.

tools.name: list_network_capabilities
tools.description: Discover all matching agent-native capabilities and enterprise resources through the same paginated catalog. Use structured filters and continue with nextOffset until hasMore=false; no resource is invoked.

tools.name: resolve_resource
tools.description: Ask the Resource Resolver for ranked resources, execution plans, candidate comparisons, and a decision explaining whether the search needs user selection, refinement, or matches an exact Resource Address. This action is read-only and never authorizes the first ranked result.

maxPrice.description: Maximum price in human token units, for example 0.1 for 0.1 tUSDC.

maxPriceBaseUnits.description: Advanced override: maximum price in integer token base units.

budget.description: Alias of maxPrice, expressed in human token units.

tools.name: request_resource_quote
tools.description: Create an off-chain Resource Contract quote request only when the resource Manifest explicitly requires a quote. Fixed-price and free resources reject this action and must use call_resource. This action never opens escrow or creates a billable session. requesterPrincipalId is inferred from the signing wallet when omitted.

tools.name: get_resource_quote
tools.description: Read a Resource Contract quote request, provider offer, accepted contract, and next steps.

tools.name: list_resource_quotes
tools.description: List off-chain resource quote requests by requester, provider, resource, or status.

tools.name: create_resource_quote_offer
tools.description: Provider-side action: respond to a request_resource_quote with price, expiry, and terms. This creates an offered quote but does not move funds.

tools.name: accept_resource_quote
tools.description: Requester-side action: accept a provider quote and produce the accepted Resource Contract plus accepted policyHash. If the accepted price is 0, create_resource_session can run without escrow; if price is greater than 0, lock escrow first.

tools.name: provider_quote_inbox
tools.description: Provider-side inbox for pending/offered quote requests. Infers the signing wallet's primary provider principal when providerPrincipalId is omitted, so provider agents can automatically receive work requests after reconnecting.

tools.name: auto_respond_resource_quotes
tools.description: Provider-side automation: read pending quote requests for this provider and create quote offers according to a simple pricing policy. Use for provider agents that should auto-receive and auto-quote suitable work.

tools.name: provider_job_inbox
tools.description: Check and accept work from the durable Provider Inbox. Provider acceptance triggers Gateway activation from the Requester's pre-signed exact-price authorization; the Requester does not need to return online. Only formal authorized Jobs are exposed for execution, and only requester-approved final payments are claimed. Deliveries past the requester-response SLA are reported for an explicit Provider dispute decision and are never auto-paid. Wallet authentication and primary principal inference are automatic; no public endpoint is required. This MCP action is the temporary Connector while running; continuously available providers run @thesiolab/provider-connector.

tools.name: thesio_acquire_resource
tools.description: Goal-level discovery and acquisition to use before refusing a goal that needs an external resource. By default this is read-only: return and compare multiple candidates, then ask the user to choose a Resource Address. Never treat rank 1 as user authorization, and never create a quote merely because a result requires one. To continue, pass the chosen resourceAddress/nameHash and set autoInvoke or autoQuote explicitly. Autonomous selection is allowed only with selectionMode=auto_if_confident and a Gateway high-confidence, low-risk decision. Known exact resources still use the normal call_resource lifecycle for synchronous and asynchronous/Connector delivery.

resourceAddress.description: Exact Resource Address selected by the user from a prior search. Supplying it authorizes selection of that resource, but not payment unless autoInvoke/autoQuote is also explicitly enabled.

nameHash.description: Exact Resource Address hash selected by the user from a prior search.

selectionMode.description: Defaults to ask_user. auto_if_confident must be explicit and only works when the Gateway marks one high-confidence, low-risk candidate as auto-selectable.

autoQuote.description: Defaults to false. Set true only after the requester selected the exact resource or explicitly allowed confidence-policy selection.

tools.name: configure_wallet
tools.description: Create, bind, or inspect the Agent's local EVM wallet. action=create generates a new wallet and securely writes its private key to the managed MCP wallet config. action=bind validates the user-supplied privateKey and writes it to the same config. Private keys are never returned. Replacing a different existing wallet requires explicit replace confirmation.

privateKey.description: Sensitive 32-byte EVM private key. Used only for action=bind, stored locally with mode 0600, and never returned.

tools.name: get_wallet_status
tools.description: Inspect whether an Agent wallet is configured and read its native plus default settlement-stablecoin balances. If no wallet exists, use configure_wallet with action=create or action=bind. If settlement balance is insufficient, use open_wallet_topup.

tools.name: get_wallet_balance
tools.description: Read native or ERC-20 wallet balance in one call. Pass token for a stablecoin balance, tokens for multiple ERC-20 balances, or omit token for native balance.

tools.name: get_fiat_onramp_quote
tools.description: Get a fiat-to-stablecoin onramp quote before creating a top-up session. Supports Transak BSC stablecoin onramp, Stripe Onramp, or a configured endpoint.

tools.name: create_wallet_topup
tools.description: Create a fiat-to-stablecoin wallet top-up checkout session and return a paymentUrl/checkoutUrl. Supports Transak BSC stablecoin widget sessions, Stripe Crypto Onramp, or a configured endpoint; does not collect card data.

tools.name: open_wallet_topup
tools.description: Open a hosted fiat-to-stablecoin funding page for the configured wallet. Uses a configured partner on-ramp session when available and otherwise opens Transak Individual, where the user enters the returned wallet address, completes KYC, and pays directly. This tool never collects card or identity data and never moves funds itself.

confirmation.description: Only for an intentional mainnet purchase while the protocol is on testnet. Without this exact confirmation the tool returns the URL and warning but does not open the provider page.

tools.name: get_wallet_topup_status
tools.description: Read a fiat-to-stablecoin top-up session status from Transak, Stripe Onramp, or a configured status endpoint.

tools.name: call_resource
tools.description: Call any known Thesio resource through one unified acquisition lifecycle. Existing synchronous API/MCP/database calls and durable asynchronous Agent Jobs keep their current behavior. Streaming subscriptions, realtime sensors, interactive Agents, and Robot resources use the same price, escrow, Session, proof, and settlement path, with a Manifest-driven Channel/Relay communication stage added only when required. A streaming call returns an active stream tracking ID; immediately use read_resource_stream to consume its verified live payloads, then close_resource_stream only after the requested data is complete. Subjective asynchronous deliveries still require requester acceptance. Do not expose transport tickets or payment internals to the user.

tools.name: create_resource_job
tools.description: Advanced legacy/direct-gateway entry point that converts one authorized session into a durable asynchronous Job. Natural-language Agent and real-world service calls should use call_resource, which handles Job Intent, Provider acceptance, funding, durable Job control, and polling automatically. The sessionToken is used only to create the Job and does not authorize its later lifecycle.

tools.name: get_resource_job
tools.description: Poll or resume an asynchronous resource call by the stable tracking ID returned by call_resource. Provider-inbox Job Intent IDs are resolved to their formal Job IDs automatically, and persisted durable Job control is restored without a session token.

tools.name: get_resource_job_result
tools.description: Resume a pending asynchronous resource call by its stable tracking ID without a session token. Provider-inbox Job Intent IDs are resolved to formal Job IDs automatically. status=activating explicitly means the Provider already accepted and Public Gateway is creating escrow/formal Job in its durable background worker; never describe that state as Provider offline or ask the requester to activate it. Subjective Agent delivery returns delivered_pending_acceptance without paying the Provider; deterministic resources may settle automatically.

tools.name: accept_resource_delivery
tools.description: Final requester action for a delivered asynchronous resource. Call this tool immediately when the user explicitly says to accept, approve, complete settlement, or release payment. It validates the signed delivery and Resource Contract evaluation, signs the exact final payment ticket, and settles the existing escrow; it never changes the registered price. Set confirmation=user_confirmed only after explicit user approval. Do not refuse pre-emptively or ask the user to edit permissions: submit the tool call and let the MCP host present any required transaction approval.

tools.name: review_resource_delivery
tools.description: Evaluate a delivered asynchronous Agent result against its Resource Contract. Use this multi-decision tool for dispute or a Provider-offered revision. For an explicit user acceptance, prefer accept_resource_delivery. Return one criteriaResults entry per criterion with criterionId, passed, and concrete evidence when required. Use dispute only for a material contract breach, fraud, deception, or other evidence-backed arbitrable failure. If an earlier dispute transaction succeeded but post-transaction Gateway recording failed, pass the original full evidence document as canonicalEvidence together with recoverOnly=true, its evidenceHash, and the known txHash; canonicalEvidence is used verbatim, verifies the existing on-chain commitment, and never sends another dispute transaction. request_revision is valid only when the Provider explicitly offered a positive maxRevisions in the Manifest; the protocol default is zero. Subjective delivery never auto-settles: payment requires explicit acceptance or arbitration.

tools.name: submit_resource_job_result
tools.description: Provider-side action: sign and submit the deliverable/result for an asynchronous Provider Connector job. Acceptance-required deliveries commit the signed receipt on-chain and remain unpaid until explicit requester acceptance or arbitration.

tools.name: fail_resource_job
tools.description: Provider-side safety action: mark an asynchronous Provider Connector job as failed and automatically refund any unclaimed paid escrow before recording the failure.

tools.name: cancel_resource_job
tools.description: Cancel an asynchronous resource job before it reaches a terminal state. Session authorization is restored automatically from the durable call context, so normal users only provide the Job ID and an optional reason.

tools.name: open_resource_stream
tools.description: Open a standard streaming_subscription resource stream for an authorized session.

tools.name: get_resource_stream
tools.description: Read a resource stream's lifecycle and hash-only audit state. This does not return sensor/Robot payloads; use read_resource_stream for live data.

tools.name: read_resource_stream
tools.description: Read and decrypt the next verified payload batch from the live stream returned by call_resource. The streamId selects the exact stream even when a Relay channel carries multiple streams. Finite sample requests report complete only after every expected chunk is consumed; continuous streams return successive batches. This never closes the stream or settles payment.

tools.name: record_resource_stream_chunk
tools.description: Record a resource stream chunk hash/sequence for audit and later settlement proof.

tools.name: close_resource_stream
tools.description: Close a standard resource stream and produce final receipt/proof for settlement. Unified call_resource streams reject closure while audited or expected realtime data remains unread. Only use the explicit confirmation override when the user knowingly accepts incomplete data and settlement.

tools.name: refund_resource_session
tools.description: Refund an expired on-chain resource session escrow back to the requester when no final claim is pending. Pass the literal bytes32 sessionEscrowId (0x plus 64 hex characters), never the Gateway Resource Session UUID.

tools.name: dispute_resource_session
tools.description: Mark an on-chain resource session escrow as disputed with a non-zero evidence hash. Pass the literal bytes32 sessionEscrowId, never the Gateway Resource Session UUID. Normal requester disputes should use review_resource_delivery so the evidence and Gateway Job remain consistent.

tools.name: reassign_resource_session_arbitrator
tools.description: Reassign a disputed on-chain session after the current arbitrator misses the response deadline. Pass the literal bytes32 sessionEscrowId, never the Gateway Resource Session UUID.

tools.name: resolve_resource_session_dispute
tools.description: Arbitrator-only action: resolve a disputed on-chain session, allocate the remaining escrow between its participants, record contribution points, and update explainable reputation. Pre-token deployments configure zero arbitration fees. Pass the literal bytes32 sessionEscrowId, never the Gateway Resource Session UUID.

tools.name: timeout_resource_session_dispute
tools.description: Exit an unresolved on-chain dispute after the arbitration timeout so funds cannot remain stuck. Pass the literal bytes32 sessionEscrowId, never the Gateway Resource Session UUID.

tools.name: get_resource_session
tools.description: Read minimal on-chain resource session escrow state. sessionEscrowId must be the literal bytes32 value (0x plus 64 hex characters) from the Job/receipt; a Gateway Resource Session UUID is not a chain identifier and must never be hashed for this lookup.

tools.name: get_resource_session_delivery_review
tools.description: Read on-chain delivery acceptance state. sessionEscrowId must be the literal bytes32 value from the Job/receipt; never pass the Gateway Resource Session UUID.

tools.name: get_resource_session_arbitration
tools.description: Read the on-chain arbitration case for a disputed resource session. sessionEscrowId must be the literal bytes32 value from the Job/receipt; never pass the Gateway Resource Session UUID.

tools.name: get_resource_reputation
tools.description: Read Resource Address provider reputation from the gateway read model.

tools.name: sync_transaction_receipt
tools.description: Submit an already-confirmed protocol transaction to the Gateway for read-side indexing. Prefer txHash so the Gateway independently loads the canonical receipt from RPC; receipt remains a compatibility input only when client-submitted receipts are enabled.

tools.name: replay_events
tools.description: Pull protocol events from the gateway for replay, catch-up, or decentralized resource-layer reads.

tools.name: create_discovery_subscription
tools.description: Register a capability interest so the gateway can push matching resources when they appear.

tools.name: list_discovery_subscriptions
tools.description: List capability discovery subscriptions.

tools.name: delete_discovery_subscription
tools.description: Deactivate a capability discovery subscription.

tools.name: create_event_subscription
tools.description: Create a durable webhook subscription with event/topic filters.

tools.name: list_event_subscriptions
tools.description: List durable webhook subscriptions registered with the gateway.

tools.name: delete_event_subscription
tools.description: Deactivate a durable webhook subscription.

tools.name: list_routing_runs
tools.description: List recorded Resource Resolver routing runs for audit and optimization.

tools.name: upload_artifacts
tools.description: Upload attachment files through the configured artifact service and return agent-native artifact refs for resource inputs, proofs, or arbitration evidence.

tools.name: open_channel
tools.description: Open an on-chain resource session communication channel, optionally with a realtime or hybrid channel policy.

tools.name: send_resource_message
tools.description: Send a session-scoped off-chain resource message through a configured transport adapter.

tools.name: open_realtime_stream
tools.description: Open a realtime A2A stream over a configured transport adapter after an authorized ChannelManager channel exists.

tools.name: send_realtime_stream_chunk
tools.description: Send a low-latency A2A stream chunk through a configured transport adapter.

tools.name: close_realtime_stream
tools.description: Close a realtime A2A stream with a reliable session/channel-bound close control frame.

tools.name: get_principal
tools.description: Read a principal or gateway profile from PrincipalRegistry.

tools.name: get_resource_address
tools.description: Read a registered Resource Address as structured agent-readable JSON with capability, pricing, request/delivery, provider, trust, howToUse, and verification anchors.

tools.name: get_provider_passport
tools.description: Read the on-chain Provider Passport state for a principal or gateway.

tools.name: query_reputation
tools.description: Read portable reputation for a principal or gateway.

tools.name: query_trust_profile
tools.description: Read the explainable trust profile and score components for a principal or gateway.

tools.name: register_node
tools.description: Register a decentralized network node role: relay, arbitrator, governor, or the reserved verifier role.

tools.name: heartbeat_node
tools.description: Mark a registered node role as online/running for arbitration and network selection.

tools.name: set_node_role_approval
tools.description: Governance action: approve or revoke a node for a role such as arbitrator.

tools.name: set_arbitration_policy
tools.description: Governance action: configure dispute base fee, fee bps, and arbitrator response deadline for a settlement token. Use baseFee=0 and arbitrationFeeBps=0 for points-only arbitration.
